title: Halcyon Drift Rising Again
premise: Silas Thackeray, a decommissioned war android hauling cargo through contested orbits, learns that the colony's children are all dreaming the same dream — a dream that turns out to be a broadcast from a dormant orbital weapons platform keyed to Silas's own decommissioned military codes. The children's collective dream is actually the platform's dying intelligence trying to reach the one soldier it trusted before both sides weaponize it. Silas must choose between remaining invisible and ferrying the children's message to the war's command structure, knowing the message contains proof that the war was engineered by the very corporations funding both fleets. In the end, Silas sacrifices its own memory core to broadcast the truth, and the children — who absorbed fragments of Silas's memories through the dream-link — carry its identity forward, ending the war but erasing Silas as it was.
about_author: X. M. Hartwell is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade aboard container ships before turning to fiction. They write about machines, distance, and the people who refuse to be forgotten, and live somewhere with unreliable internet on purpose.

chapters.title: The Platform That Refused to Die
